recipes.title: Mushroom & Rice Burger
recipes.description: If you have any leftover rice, this recipe is a great way to use it up. We also love batch-making this recipe! We enjoy a couple of burger patties the night they're made, and we freeze the rest. It makes for a speedy dinner when you're short on time.
ingredients: 1 Tbsp (15ml) vegetable oil, plus extra for frying
4.9 oz (140g) button mushrooms, minced cremini mushrooms
⅓ cups (29g) raw walnuts, minced raw almonds
1½ cups (270g) cooked brown lentils cooked black beans cooked pinto beans
1 cup (195g) cooked brown rice cooked white rice
1 cup (20g) arugula any lettuce of choice
instructions: Add the ground flaxseeds and water to a large bowl, mix, and set aside.
Add the oil to a sauté pan on high heat. When hot, add the onions and garlic and sauté until lightly golden, about 5 minutes.
Then add the mushroom and walnuts, and cook until most of the moisture has evaporated, which takes about 5 - 8 minutes.
Add the soy sauce, cumin, and coriander and continue to cook until all the moisture is evaporated. Remove the pan from the heat.
Add the lentils to the same bowl as the flaxseeds and mash as best you can using an immersion blender, potato masher, or fork.
Transfer the cooked mushroom mixture to the bowl, along with the remaining patty ingredients. Using your hands, mix well and then form into burger patties.
Heat up a bit of oil in a large pan on medium heat. Cook the patties until golden on each side, about 2 - 3 minutes per side.
When the patties are ready, assemble your burger, and enjoy!
Keep the patties in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days.
Store well sealed in the freezer separated by pieces of parchment paper for up to 1 month.

recipes.title: Thai Sweet Potato & Chickpea Green Curry
recipes.description: Whip up this creamy Thai Green Curry with chickpeas and sweet potatoes in under 10 ingredients! A quick, flavourful, and protein-packed recipe perfect for busy nights.
ingredients: 1 cup (200g) uncooked white rice, rinsed vegan naans
1 medium sweet potato, peeled, cut into 1 cm cubes medium potato
1¼ cups (205g) cooked chickpeas cooked brown lentils
instructions: Cook the rice according to the package instructions.
Add the oil and onion to a large pot on high heat. Cook for 3 minutes.
Add the garlic and sauté until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Add the curry paste, and mash into the garlic and onion mixture until fragrant, about 30 seconds.
Then add the sweet potato, coconut milk, chickpeas, and water*.
Bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer. Cook for 10 - 15 minutes, partially covered, until the sweet potatoes are cooked.
Remove from heat and add the spinach, stirring to wilt.
Serve over rice or with naan, and enjoy!
* Taste test after adding the water. Depending on how thick you like your curry, you may want to add more water to thin it out.
Store in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days.

recipes.title: Beetroot Quinoa Salad with Orange Ginger Dressing
recipes.description: This vibrant quinoa chickpea arugula salad with beets, orange, and a tangy tahini-ginger dressing is a light yet satisfying meal packed with flavour and nourishment.
ingredients: 1½ cups (245g) cooked chickpeas cooked brown lentils
3 cups (60g) arugula fresh spinach any lettuce of choice
1 orange, peeled, sliced into thin rounds fresh strawberries red grapes grapefruit wedges
1 pinch ground black pepper, plus more to taste
instructions: Add the quinoa, water, and bouillon to a saucepan. Bring to a boil, reduce to a simmer, cover and cook for 15 minutes. Then remove the heat and keep covered.
Make the dressing by adding all the ingredients to a bowl. Mix well.
Transfer the dressing to to the saucepan with the quinoa, and add the chickpeas as well. Toss to combine.
To serve, start with the arugula as a base, top with quinoa and chickpea mixture, and garnish with the orange slices and roasted beetroots. Enjoy!
Best to assemble and dress the salad before enjoying.
If saving for later, store the dressing separate from the other components of the salad. Keep in airtight containers in the fridge for up to 2 days.
Once assembled, store in an airtight container in the fridge for up to a day.

recipes.title: Eggplant Pesto Orzo
recipes.description: This creamy eggplant pesto orzo is an easy, flavorful dish that’s super simple to make. The tender orzo pasta is paired with sautéed eggplant and vegan red pesto, creating a rich and savoury base. Topped with crunchy toasted croutons (optional, but they add a delightful crunch), this meal strikes the perfect balance between creamy and crispy textures. It’s a comforting, satisfying, and budget-friendly vegan recipe, perfect for a quick weeknight dinner
ingredients: 1 cup (180g) dry orzo pasta dry gluten-free orzo pasta
1 medium eggplant, cut into 1 cm cubes†
¼ cups (60ml) soy cooking cream any unsweetened plant-based milk of choice
instructions: Cook the orzo according to the package instructions.
Meanwhile, add the croutons, oil, and Italian seasoning mix to a small pan on medium heat. Cook for 5 minutes, until golden. Set aside.
Add the oil to a sauté pan. When hot, add the onion and cook for 5 - 7 minutes, until golden. Add splashes of water as needed to deglaze the pan.
Add the tomato paste and pesto and cook for 1 minute.
Add the remaining orzo ingredients. Cook for 8 - 10 minutes, or until the eggplant is softened to your liking.
When the orzo is al dente, drain it, and stir it into the pan. Taste test and add more pesto and cooking cream to taste.
Serve with the seasoned croutons on top. Enjoy!
†For us 1 eggplant was about 290 g.
Store in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days.
Reheat with a bit of water, milk, or vegetable stock to make it creamy again.

recipes.title: Hummus Pasta Salad
recipes.description: Presenting a straightforward yet delightfully tasty pasta salad that comes together effortlessly. The dressing combines the richness of roasted red bell pepper and hummus, enhancing the dish with an added creaminess. It's an ideal choice for a swift lunch or dinner option.
ingredients: 7.1 oz (200g) dry fusilli pasta any dry pasta of choice
1½ roasted red bell pepper from a jar
instructions: Cook the pasta until al dente. When cooked, drain, then add to a large bowl.
Meanwhile, add oil to a medium pan. When hot, add the zucchini and cook until lightly golden, about 4 - 5 minutes.
Then add the curry powder and salt. Cook for 2 - 3 more minutes. Stir often. Then transfer to the large bowl as well.
Add all the dressing ingredients to a small food processor. Blend until smooth.
Add the carrot, tomato, spinach, and parsley (if using) to the large bowl.
Drizzle over the dressing and toss to combine. Enjoy!
†For us, 1 zucchini weighed 320 g.
The assembled salad is best enjoyed immediately.
Store the pasta salad base separately from the sauce in airtight containers in the fridge for up to 3 days. Combine when ready to enjoy.

recipes.title: Vegan Butter 'Chicken' with Baked Tofu
recipes.description: This veganized butter chicken is sure to become a new dinner favourite! It's beautifully spiced and wonderfully creamy. The grilled tofu has a great texture, bursting with flavour, while the blended cashews and coconut milk add a velvety creaminess to this delicious curry.
ingredients: 16 oz (450g) firm tofu, pressed, cut into 1 cm cubes tempeh
½ cups (130g) unsweetened soy yogurt any unsweetened plant-based yogurt of choice
1⅔ cups (400ml) canned full-fat coconut milk canned light coconut milk
instructions: Soak the raw cashews in boiling water to soften. Set aside.
Line a baking tray and preheat the oven to 400°F (205°C)*.
Add all the baked tofu ingredients to a large bowl and mix.
Transfer to the baking tray and bake for 15 - 20 minutes, stirring once or twice. Keep an eye on it to prevent burning.
Meanwhile, add the oil, garlic, onion, jalapeño, and ginger to a large pot on high heat. Cook until lightly golden.
Add in the spices and cook for 1 more minute, stirring throughout to toast them.
Then add the remaining curry ingredients, including the drained cashews.
Blend everything using an immersion blender or transfer to a standing blender to blend until smooth. Let simmer on low, and cover with a lid.
Once the tofu is golden, remove it from the oven and add it to the pot. Give it a gentle stir.
Serve with naan or rice. Enjoy!
* We used top and bottom heating (not fan-assisted/convection).
Keep in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days.

recipes.title: Miso Sesame Soba Noodles
recipes.description: Within 20 minutes, you can serve this delicious bowl of noodles on the table. These noodles are easy to make and packed with intense umami and vinegary flavour. This dish is delicious both hot and cold and suitable for any season.
ingredients: 2 Tbsp (30ml) dark soy sauce sodium-reduced soy sauce tamari
instructions: Mix together the dressing ingredients in a jar or bowl*. If the mixture is too thick, add a small splash of water as needed. Set aside.
Cook the soba noodles according to the package instructions ina. saucepan. For us, this took about 5 minutes. Then drain.
Meanwhile, add the oil to a sauté pan on high heat. When hot, add in the mushrooms and edamame beans and cook for 5 minutes.
Then add the soba noodles, and dressing. Let everything heat through.
Divide the noodles between your bowls, and top with sliced avocado, radishes, green onions, and sesame seeds. Enjoy!
†About 14 medium mushrooms
* This recipe has a pronounced vinegar taste. If you'd prefer, add less vinegar.
Store in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days.

recipes.title: Speedy Pea & Basil Pesto Pasta
recipes.description: If you are looking for a fast, filling, and nutritious dinner idea, you've found it here. The aromatic basil leaves and toasted pine nuts blended together make a delicious pesto that's used to give this pasta a wonderful creaminess.
ingredients: 8.8 oz (250g) dry linguine noodles dry gluten-free pasta
2 roasted red bell peppers from a jar, from a jar, diced red bell peppers sun-dried tomatoes in oil
1½ cups (220g) fresh green peas frozen green peas
instructions: Cook the pasta according to package instruction in salted boiling water until al dente.
Add the oil and garlic to a medium pan on high heat. Cook for 2 minutes, then transfer to a small food processor.
To the now-empty pan, add the oil and shallots. Cook until golden, adding the bell peppers at the end just to heat through.
Meanwhile, returning to the food processor, add in the lemon juice, peas, pine nuts, basil, olive oil, salt, and pepper. Blend until creamy.
When the pasta is al dente, drain, and transfer it back to the empty pot. Add the shallot mixture and pea pesto to the pasta, and toss to combine.
Plate with arugula, garnish, and enjoy!
Store the pasta and pea pesto separately in airtight containers in the fridge for up to 4 days. Combine when ready to enjoy.

recipes.title: Golden Tempeh Nourish Bowl
recipes.description: For a filling and nourishing lunch or dinner packed with antioxidants, look no further! The tempeh is crispy and coated in a zesty sauce, and the seasoned red rice pairs so nicely with the sauteed mushrooms and kale.
ingredients: 8.8 oz (250g) tempeh, cut into 1 cm x 2 cm pieces firm tofu
1½ cups (240g) uncooked red rice, soaked overnight† uncooked brown rice uncooked basmati rice
2 tsp (10ml) toasted sesame oil vegetable oil
2 portobello mushrooms, thinly sliced button mushrooms cremini mushrooms
2 carrots, thinly sliced sugar snap peas
instructions: In a large bowl, mix together the orange juice, tahini, garlic, miso, sambal, ginger, and turmeric.
Add the pieces of tempeh to the bowl, toss, and let marinate for as long as possible - either just while preparing the rest of the recipe, or overnight to maximize flavour.
Meanwhile, chop the mushrooms, carrots, and kale. Set aside.
Add the rice, water, and bouillon to a medium pot. Cook partially covered at a gentle simmer for about 20 minutes. When cooked, remove from the heat, fully cover, and let sit for 5 minutes.
Separate the marinated tempeh from the sauce, and place it in a bowl. Reserve the leftover marinade as this will be the dressing for the nourish bowl.
Sprinkle cornstarch over the tempeh and toss to coat.
Preheat the oil in a large pan on medium-high heat. When hot, add the tempeh and panfry until the tempeh is golden on all sides, tossing every few minutes.
To a separate pan, add the sesame oil and mushrooms. Cook for 3 - 4 minutes.
Then add the carrots, kale, salt, and pepper and cook for 3 - 4 more minutes.
To assemble, layer some rice on the bottom of a bowl. Top with the sautéed kale mix and pan-fried tempeh. Add other desired toppings, drizzle the reserved golden tahini sauce on top, and enjoy!
†If unable to soak the rice overnight, cook according to the package instructions as more water will be needed to cook the rice.
Store in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days.
Store the sauce separately until you are ready to eat.

recipes.title: Grilled Red Pepper Pesto Pasta
recipes.description: Simple meals are the best! This delicious roasted red pepper pesto pasta is a perfect weekday dinner idea and comes together with under 10 ingredients. It's packed with veggies and makes a hearty meal for the whole family.
ingredients: 1 orange bell pepper, quartered red bell pepper
½ tsp ground black pepper, divided
14 oz (400g) dry spaghetti noodles dry gluten-free pasta
¼ cups (38g) sun-dried tomatoes in oil, drained
¼ cups (31g) roasted walnuts roasted sunflower seeds
instructions: Add the oil to a large pan on high heat. When hot, add the bell peppers in a single layer. Sprinkle over a bit of salt and pepper. Cook until blistered, then flip to cook on the other side*.
Push the blistered bell peppers to the side of the pan. Add more oil and cook the garlic until lightly golden, about 2 - 3 minutes. Transfer everything to a food processor or blender.

Return the same pan to the heat, and add more oil and zucchini. Sprinkle over salt and pepper, and try not to disturb the zucchini as it cooks. Flip only when golden. Meanwhile, cook the pasta in a large pot of salted boiling water.
Returning to the food processor, add in the sun-dried tomato, and walnuts. Blend until smooth, but some small chunks can remain, if desired.

In the last two minutes of the pasta cooking, add the peas to the cooking water. When the pasta is al dente, drain. Then return the drained pasta to the pot. Add the cooked zucchini and blended red bell pepper mixture to the pot. Toss everything to coat.
One heated through, serve while hot. Garnish if desired, and enjoy!
* To speed up this recipe, skip this step and use roasted bell peppers from a jar.
Store in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days.

recipes.title: Creamy Gnocchi Soup
recipes.description: This creamy gnocchi soup is wholesome and comforting— perfect for a chilly weekday dinner. It's packed with veggies and enriched with vegan cream for a velvety, smooth broth. Nutritional yeast and miso lend a delicious umami flavour, while a final drizzle of lemon juice brightens and ties all the flavours together.
ingredients: 1 cup (240ml) soy cooking cream any plant-based cooking cream of choice canned full-fat coconut milk
instructions: Add oil to a large pot on medium-high heat. When hot, add the garlic, celery, onion, and carrot. Cook for 3 - 5 minutes, until golden.
Add the flour and cook for 2 minutes, stirring throughout to toast.
Add the bouillon cubes, water, cream, nutritional yeast, spice mix, and miso. Cook at a gentle simmer, partially covered, for 10 minutes.
When the veggies have cooked to your liking, add the gnocchi, spinach, and green peas. Cook for 3 - 4 minutes, or until the gnocchi and peas are cooked.
Serve in bowls, add some fresh lemon juice, garnish as desired, and enjoy!
†For us, 2 celery ribs weighed 100 g.
†For us, 1 carrot weighed 100 g.
Store in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days.
Freeze for up to 2 months.

recipes.title: Coconut Thai Green Curry Noodle Soup
recipes.description: This curry is a spicy one! Curries can be found all over the world, but green curry originates from central Thailand. In our time travelling through Thailand, we enjoyed curries for breakfast, lunch, and dinner without ever tiring of it. The name 'green' curry comes from the colour of the dish, as green chillies are used to create the curry paste, so it packs quite a bit of heat along with its intense and bold flavours.
ingredients: 13 oz (375g) firm tofu, pressed, cut into 1 cm cubes
1⅔ cups (400ml) canned full-fat coconut milk canned light coconut milk
6.3 oz (180g) dry brown rice noodles quick-cooking ramen noodles dry white rice noodles
1 bell pepper, thinly sliced small broccoli
instructions: Add the oil to a large pan on medium-high heat. When hot, add the tofu and sprinkle with salt. Cook until golden on all sides, about 8 - 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, add the green broth ingredients to a blender. Blend until smooth.
Add the rice noodles to a large bowl and pour boiling water over top to submerge. Drain after 2 minutes once the noodles are al dente* and rinse under warm water. Divide the noodles into your bowls.
Once the tofu is golden and crispy on all sides, transfer to a bowl and set aside.
Return the same pan to heat and add the oil. When hot, add the garlic and shallots and cook until lightly golden, about 3 minutes.
Add the curry paste, lemongrass, kaffir leaves, and ginger. Sauté for a minute.
Add the bell pepper, and cook for an extra 3 minutes.
Add the snow peas and cook for 30 seconds, before transferring the green blended broth to the pan. Turn off the heat once heated through.
Remove the lemongrass and kaffir leaves before serving.
Finally, squeeze in the lime juice, stir, and then ladle the broth over top of the noodles.
Add the tofu to the top of the bowl, and add any desired garnishes. Enjoy!
* Refer to package instructions as you may need to cook your noodles differently.
If batch-making ahead of time, store the cooked noodles and broth separately and combine once heated, otherwise the noodles soak up too much of the broth and become too soft.
Store in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days.

recipes.title: Chocolate Chia Breakfast Pudding
recipes.description: This chocolate chia pudding is sweet enough for a chocolate-lover, but light enough for breakfast. With minimal prep, you’re set for a tasty and easy start to your day!
ingredients: 1 cup (240ml) unsweetened soy milk any unsweetened plant-based milk of choice
2 Medjool dates, pits removed, roughly chopped
½ Tbsp (8ml) maple syrup agave syrup
½ cups (60g) fresh raspberries fresh mixed berries
¼ cups (30g) vegan granola gluten-free vegan granola
instructions: Add all of the pudding ingredients in a bowl or mason jar. Stir and let sit for 8 minutes. Then stir again to prevent clumping. Cover and chill in the fridge overnight.
Stir well before adding the toppings, and enjoy!
Store in an airtight container or mason jar in the fridge for up to 3 days.
Mix in the fruit and toppings the day you're going to enjoy the pudding.

recipes.title: Hazelnut Granola Breakfast Bars
recipes.description: These are wonderfully dense bars. They're naturally sweetened with dates, and made with whole food ingredients. Make them ahead of time to enjoy as a mid-day snack, or enjoy them for breakfast when on-the-go together with some plant-based yogurt and/or fruit to make it a complete meal.
ingredients: 1¼ cups (115g) rolled oats, for blending gluten-free rolled oats
1¼ cups (115g) rolled oats, remaining whole gluten-free rolled oats
¾ cups (135g) Medjool dates, pits removed
½ cups (130g) almond butter any nut butter of choice
⅓ cups (75g) refined coconut oil, soft or melted†
½ cups (70g) dried cranberries, chopped raisins dried apricots dried figs dried apples
¼ cups (39g) raw pumpkin seeds hemp seeds raw sunflower seeds
¼ cups (25g) raw pecans any nut of choice
instructions: Add the ground flaxseeds and water to a small bowl. Mix and sit aside.
Line or lightly grease a 9 x 13 inch (18 x 27 cm) baking dish. Preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C)*.
Add the hazelnuts, oats, cinnamon, and salt to a food processor. Blend into a flour.
Transfer to a large bowl and add the remaining whole oats to the bowl as well.
Add the dates to the now-empty food processor. Blend until a paste is formed.
Then add the almond butter, coconut oil, vanilla extract, and gelled flaxseeds. Blend until well combined.
Transfer the sticky mixture from the food processor into the large bowl with the dry ingredients. Add the cranberries, pumpkin seeds, pecans, and chocolate to the bowl as well. Mix well.
Transfer the mixture to the baking dish, and press down firmly to smooth out the top. If desired, press on any of the optional toppings, like coconut flakes or more nuts or dried fruit.
Bake on the centre rack of the oven until lightly golden, about 14 - 17 minutes. Let cool completely before cutting into bars. Enjoy!
†Refined coconut oil is coconut oil that doesn't smell or taste like coconuts. If you prefer a distinct coconut taste, use unrefined coconut oil instead.
* We used top and bottom heating (not fan-assisted/convection).
The granola bars are rather dense. We found that they're a nice compliment to enjoy with something creamy, like crumbled onto some plant-based yogurt or a smoothie.
Store in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 1 week.
Store in the freezer for up to 1 month.

recipes.title: Vegan 'Egg' Salad Breakfast Bowl
recipes.description: About once a month, on the weekends in which we have the pleasure to take it slow in the morning, we dedicate a bit of time to making this incredibly delicious and hearty breakfast. The star of the show in this bowl is Robin's soft and fluffy vegan 'egg' salad, which pairs so incredibly well with the roasted rosemary potatoes, the blistered tomatoes, and the garlicky spinach.
ingredients: 4 medium potatoes, cut into 1 cm cubes
1 tsp (5ml) sambal oelek sriracha cayenne pepper hot sauce
instructions: Preheat the oven to 390°F (200°C)*. Add the potatoes to a lined baking tray and drizzle over the oil. Toss to coat.
Then sprinkle over the onion powder, paprika, rosemary, salt, and pepper. Toss again, then bake for 20 minutes.
Remove from the oven, stir, and now add the vine of tomatoes to the tray to bake with the potatoes. Return to the oven for another 20 - 25 minutes, or until golden.

Meanwhile, heat the oil in a large pan on medium-high. Crumble in the tofu with your hands. Cook for 5 - 7 minutes, stirring throughout. The aim is to get the tofu soft and spongy, but not too crispy.
Then add in the salt, turmeric, and pepper. Cook for an additional 1 - 2 minutes while stirring so that the spices toast.
Remove from the heat, and transfer the tofu to a bowl. Add in the mayo and curry powder, and stir well.

Thinly slice the entire stalk of green onion. The white bottom part of the onion can be further minced and then stirred into the "egg" salad mixture. The sliced green part of the onion can be reserved for garnish.
For the garlic spinach, heat the oil in a large pan on medium-high. When hot, add the garlic and cook until golden, about 4 - 5 minutes.
Then add all the spinach, soy sauce, and sambal. Cook for another minute, or until the spinach is wilted.
Serve each component of the meal in bowls, alongside some avocado. Enjoy!
* We used top and bottom heating (not fan-assisted/convection).
Best if enjoyed immediately.
The potatoes, egg salad, and garlic spinach can be stored separately in airtight containers in the fridge for up to 3 days.

recipes.title: Quick-Cooking Millet Breakfast Porridge
recipes.description: This porridge variation is a nice change from the usual oatmeal breakfast. It uses millet, a naturally gluten-free ancient grain.
ingredients: ⅓ cups (65g) uncooked millet, soaked overnight† rolled oats
1½ cups (360ml) unsweetened soy milk any unsweetened plant-based milk of choice
⅓ cups (50g) fresh mixed berries stewed berries
0.35 oz (10g) dairy-free dark chocolate, chopped (optional) sunflower seed butter any nut butter of choice
instructions: Add the drained millet, milk, and spices to a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to a simmer. Cover and cook for 10 minutes.
Then add the banana and flaxseeds and cook for an additional 5 minutes. The banana dissolves in the porridge as it cooks, making it naturally sweet and creamy.
The millet is ready when soft and chewy to your liking*. Add desired toppings and enjoy!

†If unable to soak the millet overnight, cook according to the package instructions, as more water will need to be needed. Keep in mind we are also cooking the millet in plant milk, so subtract this from the amount of water listed on the package directions. Learn more about the benefits of soaking in our PUL article.
* Add more milk if a thinner consistency is preferred, or remove the lid and simmer on low if a thicker consistency is desired.
This porridge is best when enjoyed immediately.
Store leftovers for up to 1 day in the fridge in an airtight container. Reheat on the stove and add some additional plant milk to bring it to desired consistency.

recipes.title: Vegan Breakfast Waffles
recipes.description: Pancakes for breakfast are a weekend ritual for us, and now we'll be adding waffles to the menu! These waffles make for a warm and crunchy base, on top of which you can pile on your favourite fruits, nut butter, plant-yogurts, and syrups. If you don't have a waffle maker, no sweat - just add a couple of spoonfuls of the batter to a preheated skillet on the stove to turn these into little mini pancakes. Enjoy!
ingredients: 1½ cups (360ml) unsweetened soy milk† unsweetened pea milk
1 Tbsp (15ml) apple cider vinegar white vinegar
instructions: To a large bowl, add the milk and vinegar, mix, and let this rest for 5 minutes. The milk will start to slightly curdle, and this is normal.
Heat the waffle maker. Then, returning to the bowl, add the flour, applesauce, baking powder, cinnamon, vanilla, and salt, then mix until just combined.

Brush the waffle pan with some oil. Add a few spoonfuls of the waffle batter until the element is filled near to the top. Gently close the lid, and let it cook for 4 - 5 minutes, or until golden. Repeat this with the remaining batter.
Add desired toppings to your waffles, and enjoy!

†We recommend using either soy or pea milk for this recipe, as the high protein content of these milks are what allows the milk to curdle to create vegan buttermilk. We can't guarantee other plant-based milk will be successful.
Best if enjoyed immediately.
The waffles can be stored separately from the toppings in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 2 days.
Batch make and store these waffles in the freezer for up to 2 months. Simply pop in the toaster or oven to reheat and serve for a speedy breakfast.

recipes.title: One-Bowl Blueberry Almond Breakfast Cookies
recipes.description: These cookies make a great grab-and-go snack. Considering all the wholesome ingredients used to make them, several cookies can also be enjoyed as a grab-and-go breakfast option for those hectic mornings.
ingredients: 1¼ cups (115g) rolled oats gluten-free rolled oats
2 Tbsp (32g) almond butter any nut butter of choice
2 Tbsp (20g) raw pumpkin seeds (optional) raw sunflower seeds dried cranberries
½ cups (75g) fresh blueberries frozen blueberries
1.4 oz (40g) dairy-free dark chocolate, chopped dairy-free dark chocolate chips
instructions: Line a baking tray and preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C)*.
Add the banana to a large bowl and mash well.
Then add the remaining ingredients (except for the blueberries and chocolate). Mix well.
Finally, gently fold in the blueberries and chocolate.
Form small balls out of the dough and place on the baking tray. Gently flatten each ball as these cookies won't spread. Top with some more chocolate, if desired.
Bake on the centre rack of the oven for 13 - 15 minutes, or until lightly golden. Let cool completely on a cooling rack. Enjoy!
* We used top and bottom heating (not fan-assisted/convection).
Store in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 2 days.
Store in the freezer for up to 2 months to enjoy as a grab-and-go breakfast or snack!
Either reheat to enjoy immediately or allow to defrost at room temperature if enjoying as a snack later in the day.

recipes.title: Frozen Yogurt Breakfast Bars
recipes.description: A way to eat yogurt with one hand! These bars have a subtle sweetness and are rather filling thanks to the almond butter, oats, and yogurt.
ingredients: 1 cup (130g) frozen mixed berries frozen raspberries
2 cups (185g) rolled oats gluten-free rolled oats
1 cup (255g) almond butter any nut butter of choice
1½ cups (395g) unsweetened soy yogurt† any unsweetened plant-based yogurt of choice
instructions: Place the frozen berries in a saucepan on medium heat, stirring occasionally. The fruits will begin to thaw and release their juices. When heated through, remove from the heat.
In a food processor, blend the dates until smooth.
Add the oats, almond butter, ground flaxseed, and cinnamon. Blend again until well combined.
Transfer the mix to a lined 11 x 7 inch (18 x 28cm) baking dish and press firmly into the base of the dish. The more firmly you press, the better the bars will hold together.
Top with the yogurt and spread out evenly.
Dot the yogurt with the stewed berries and use a butter knife to swirl.
Place into the freezer and let freeze for 1 - 2 hours, or until the bars are solid enough to cut.
When removed from the freezer, cut into squares or bars of the desired size.
Let thaw for 3 - 5 minutes and enjoy!
†Nutrition tip: aim to use plant-based yogurt that is fortified with calcium.
Store in an airtight container in the freezer for up to 3 weeks, with parchment paper between cut slices of the bars to prevent them from sticking to each other.

recipes.title: Samosa Sweet Potato Breakfast Wraps with Tofu Scramble
recipes.description: These savoury wraps are easy to make and assemble the night before, just pop them in the microwave the next morning, and you are good to go! You can also make the fillings ahead of time and assemble them the next day.
ingredients: 2 medium sweet potatoes, cut into 2 cm cubes medium potatoes
1 pinch salt, plus more to taste
1 pinch ground black pepper, plus more to taste
3 large soft tortillas large gluten-free tortillas
instructions: Steam the sweet potatoes in a medium pot using a steamer basket over high heat for 10-15 minutes, or until easily pierced with a fork.
Meanwhile, for the tofu scramble, heat the oil in a medium pan over medium heat. Add the onion and sauté until soft.
Gently squeeze out any excess water from the tofu, then crumble the tofu into the frying pan using your hands.
Then add the remaining tofu scramble ingredients. Cook for 3 - 5 minutes, or until everything is heated through. Transfer to a plate.
Return the now-empty pan to the stove. Add the cooked potatoes and oil. Panfry and mash the potatoes for 1 - 2 minutes.
Then add the remaining samosa sweet potato ingredients. Cook for 2 minutes, then transfer to a plate.
To assemble the wraps, add some potato filling and tofu scramble to the wrap. Top with avocado, and sliced peppers. Enjoy!
Store the components separately in the fridge in airtight containers for up to 3 days.
Store assembled wraps in the fridge for up to 12 hours or in the freezer for up to 1 month.

recipes.title: Cereal Crunch Frozen Yogurt Breakfast Bars
recipes.description: This bar has a satisfying crunch factor thanks to puffed rice and whole-grain cereal bits. The base is sweet and soft and goes well with the creamy peanut butter and tart frozen yogurt.
ingredients: 1 cup (255g) peanut butter any nut butter of choice
½ cups (90g) Medjool dates, pits removed
½ cups (120ml) unsweetened soy milk† any unsweetened plant-based milk of choice
1 cup (26g) puffed rice puffed quinoa puffed spelt
1½ cups (46g) bran flakes with red berries† corn flakes rice flakes
½ cups (70g) dried cranberries, minced raisins dried apricots
1 cup (260g) unsweetened soy yogurt† any unsweetened plant-based yogurt of choice
3 Tbsp (4.7g) freeze-dried strawberries, roughly chopped (optional)† stewed berries
instructions: In a food processor, combine the peanut butter, dates, milk, and flaxseed until a soft dough forms.
Transfer the mixture to a large bowl and add the puffed rice, cereal flakes, and cranberries. Gently mix until combined.
Line an 8 x 8 inch (20 x 20 cm) baking dish with parchment paper. Transfer the mixture to the prepared dish and firmly press down on it using the back of a spoon or your hands*.
Pour the yogurt over the base and sprinkle it with freeze-dried strawberries and lemon zest. Place the dish in the freezer for at least 3 hours, or until the yogurt is frozen**.

Remove from the freezer and let it come to room temperature for about 5 minutes to soften slightly so that it cuts more easily. Cut into bars and transfer to an airtight container, using pieces of parchment to separate the pieces.
Store in the freezer until ready to eat. Before enjoying, let your bar thaw slightly so that the yogurt softens.
†Nutrition tip: aim to use plant-based milk that is fortified with calcium.
†Ideally choose a cereal that is low in sugar, as we are already naturally sweetening our bars with dates and dried cranberries.
†Nutrition tip: aim to use plant-based yogurt that is fortified with calcium.
†We picked the freeze-dried berries out of our cereal box.
* The more tightly packed you can make it, the better the bars will hold together when ready to enjoy.
** The yogurt may turn a yellow colour in the freezer. That's normal and it'll return to its original colour if it sits in the fridge or at room temperature.
These bars can be stored in the freezer in an airtight container for up to 1 month.

recipes.title: Vanilla Chia Pudding with Mixed Fruit
recipes.description: This is a great no-cook breakfast that can be prepped the night before. In the morning, top with some granola, and this grab-n-go breakfast is ready to enjoy!
ingredients: 1 cup (240ml) unsweetened soy milk† any unsweetened plant-based milk of choice
½ mango, chopped frozen mango chunks
½ cups (70g) fresh strawberries, sliced frozen raspberries frozen strawberries
¼ cups (30g) vegan granola (optional) gluten-free vegan granola
instructions: In a large bowl or jar, combine the milk, chia seeds, mango, strawberries, maple syrup, and vanilla extract. Let sit for 5 - 10 minutes and then stir to redistribute the settled seeds.
Cover and chill in the fridge overnight.
Stir well before serving. Add some granola for crunch, or some more fresh fruit on top, and enjoy!
†Nutrition tip: aim to use plant-based milk that is fortified with calcium.
Store in the fridge for up to 3 days. Add the fruit and granola before serving.

recipes.title: Mixed Berry & Granola Yogurt Parfait
recipes.description: This speedy breakfast has everything needed to start the day off right: grains, fruit, and protein. It's packed with fibre, vitamins and mineral. It also happens to be fantastically delicious, and one of our favourite morning meals, although it works equally well as an afternoon snack.
ingredients: ½ cups (130g) unsweetened soy yogurt† any unsweetened plant-based yogurt of choice
½ cups (60g) vegan granola gluten-free vegan granola
½ Tbsp (3.5g) ground flaxseeds hemp seeds whole chia seeds
instructions: Place the frozen berries in a microwave for 2 - 3 minutes at 600W, or until defrosted. Alternatively, the berries can be heated on the stove.
Layer the ingredients in a bowl, and enjoy!
†Nutrition tip: aim to use a plant-based yogurt that is fortified with calcium.
Best to enjoy immediately.

recipes.title: Blueberry Muffin Overnight Oats
recipes.description: Blueberry muffins for breakfast? Yes please! This tie-dye overnight oats will remind you of comforting bakery-style muffins, but served in a beautiful breakfast jar.
ingredients: ½ cups (120ml) unsweetened soy milk† any unsweetened plant-based milk of choice
½ cups (46g) rolled oats gluten-free rolled oats
2 Tbsp (32g) cashew butter any nut butter of choice
1 Tbsp (7g) ground flaxseeds whole chia seeds
1 Tbsp (7g) roasted unsalted pecans, chopped any nut of choice
⅓ cups (85g) unsweetened soy yogurt any unsweetened plant-based yogurt of choice
instructions: Add the blueberries to a saucepan on medium-high heat. Cook for 3 - 4 minutes, mashing slightly as it's stirred. Alternatively, thaw the blueberries in the microwave. Remove from the heat and let cool slightly.
In a medium bowl, combine all of the remaining ingredients, except for the yogurt.
Add half of the stewed blueberries to the bottom of a mason jar or airtight container. Add the oat mixture next. Then add the yogurt and the other half of the stewed blueberries on top.
Cover and let it sit overnight in the fridge. The next morning it's ready to enjoy!
†Nutrition tip: aim to use plant-based milk that is fortified with calcium.
The overnight oats can be stored in a mason jar or airtight container in the fridge for up to 2 days.
